'''Luís A. N. Amaral''' (born 12 July 1968) is a [[Portuguese people|Portuguese]] physicist recognized for his research in [[complex systems]] and [[complex networks]].<ref name="McCormick School of Engineering website news">{{cite web|title=McCormick School of Engineering website news|url=http://www.mccormick.northwestern.edu/news/articles/2012/11/four-mccormick-professors-named-AAAS-fellows.html|accessdate=13 June 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=JSMF Advisory members website|url=http://www.jsmf.org/programs/cs/board.htm|accessdate=21 June 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=HHMI Early Career Scientist Bio|url=http://www.hhmi.org/research/ecs/amaral_bio.html|accessdate=21 June 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130514104332/http://www.hhmi.org/research/ecs/amaral_bio.html|archive-date=14 May 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="New York Times">{{cite web|title=New York Times | website=[[Forbes]] |url=https://www.forbes.com/2010/06/16/real-madrid-world-cup-technology-breakthroughs-soccer-statistics.html?boxes=Homepagelighttop |accessdate=21 June 2013 |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20130629190255/http://www.forbes.com/2010/06/16/real-madrid-world-cup-technology-breakthroughs-soccer-statistics.html?boxes=Homepagelighttop |archivedate=29 June 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> His specific research interests include the emergence, evolution, and stability of complex social and biological systems.<ref name="Amaral Lab Website">{{cite web|title=Amaral Lab website|url=http://www.amaral-lab.org|accessdate=13 June 2013}}</ref> He is best known for his work in network classification and cartographic methods for uncovering the organization of complex networks. He is currently professor at [[McCormick School of Engineering]] and [[Feinberg School of Medicine]], [[Northwestern University]].<ref name="McCormick School of Engineering website news"/>

== Education ==

Amaral received both his bachelor's and master's degrees in physics from the [[University of Lisbon]] in 1990 and 1992, respectively. He then went to Boston, where he performed his doctoral work under the supervision of [[H. Eugene Stanley]] at [[Boston University]], and received his doctoral degree in physics in 1996. He was a postdoctoral researcher at Forschungszentrum Jülich, [[MIT]], Boston University, and [[Harvard Medical School]]. In 2002, he became a professor at [[Northwestern University]].<ref name="Amaral Lab Website"/>

== Academic career ==

Amaral has published over one hundred fifty scientific peer-reviewed papers in leading scientific journals, with more than twelve thousand citations.<ref name="Web of Science">{{cite web|title=Web of Science|url=http://apps.webofknowledge.com|accessdate=13 June 2013}}</ref> His research has been featured in many media sources. He is currently editor of several academic journals including [[Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment, Scientific Directorate and Editorial Board|url=http://iopscience.iop.org/1742-5468/page/Scientific%20Directorate%20and%20Editorial%20Board|accessdate=21 June 2013}}</ref> and [[PLoS ONE]].<ref>{{cite web|title=PLoS ONE Editorial Board|url=http://www.plosone.org/static/edboard|accessdate=21 June 2013}}</ref> He also serves as the graduate program director at the Department of Chemical Engineering at Northwestern University. He was expected to become the co-director of Northwestern Institute on Complex Systems (NICO) in the fall of 2013.<ref>{{cite web|title=NICO website News|url=http://www.nico.northwestern.edu/news/news-articles/2013/Luis%20Amaral%20to%20Become%20NICO%20Co-director.html|accessdate=13 June 2013}}</ref>

== Entrepreneurship ==

Amaral is the co-founder and scientific advisor of Chimu Solutions, Inc.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chimu Solutions website|url=http://chimusolutions.com/|accessdate=13 June 2013}}</ref> The company's main product, Footballrrating.com, tracks the performance of soccer teams and individual players.<ref name="New York Times"/> The technique is based on a paper co-authored by Amaral and the other co-founder of the company, Jordi Duch.

== Personal life ==

[[File:Sketch of Luis Amaral.jpg|thumb|A sketch of Luís Amaral by his wife, Sarah Kaiser, an artist]]
Professor Amaral currently lives in the city of [[Evanston, Illinois|Evanston]] with his wife and his two sons, Jordi and Ferran. Apart from science, he is interested in food and history. He is also an avid soccer fan, particularly for the [[Portugal national football team|Portugal national soccer team]] and [[S.L. Benfica|Sport Lisboa e Benfica]].<ref name="New York Times"/>

* Scholarship (10 years), Fundação Calouste Gulbenkian, Portugal (1981)
